entry: City in central [[Kentucky]], coterminous with Fayette County and its county seat. Known as the "Horse Capital of the World" for its hundreds of horse farms, it is home to the Kentucky Horse Park and the Keeneland and Red Mile race courses. With 322,570 residents at the 2020 census, it is the state's second most populous city after Louisville. The city has been consolidated with Fayette County since 1974 and has a nonpartisan mayor-council government. Frontiersmen named the site in June 1775, after hearing of the fighting at Lexington, Massachusetts.

Prefecture-level city and capital of the [[Tibet Autonomous Region]], China, at an average elevation of 3,650 meters on the [[Tibetan Plateau]]. The urban center lies in the basin of the Lhasa River, a tributary of the Yarlung Tsangpo, and has around 300,000 residents. The 2000 census recorded 474,490 people, of whom 387,124 were ethnic [[Tibetans]]. Herders raise yaks, sheep and goats in the uplands, while river valleys grow barley, wheat and vegetables. The Qinghai–Tibet railway terminates in the city. [[Buddhism|Tibetan Buddhism]] has shaped local culture since the 7th century, and the [[UNESCO]]-recognized Potala Palace was the winter residence of the Dalai Lamas. Most monasteries were damaged during the [[Cultural Revolution]], but many have since been restored as tourist attractions. Mining has caused environmental problems.

[[Hong Kong]] tycoon and philanthropist. Li was born in Chao'an, [[Guangdong]] Province, and his family fled to Hong Kong in 1940 as refugees from the Sino-Japanese War. After his father died of [[Tuberculosis]], he left school at 15 and worked long hours at a plastics trading company. In 1950 he founded Cheung Kong Industries, which he developed into a real estate company listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 1972. Cheung Kong acquired Hutchison Whampoa in 1979, and through CK Hutchison Holdings Li later invested in ports, telecommunications, retail and energy. He retired as chairman of CK Hutchison in 2018 and stayed on as senior advisor. Through the Li Ka Shing Foundation, established in 1980, he has committed over US$3.8 billion to education, medical research and healthcare.

Legalist philosopher and statesman of the [[Qin dynasty]] in ancient China. As chancellor of the Qin state from 246 to 208 BC, Li served first under King Zheng, later [[Qin Shi Huang]], the "First Emperor", and then under his successor. He helped standardize laws, weights and measures, currency and writing, facilitating the cultural unification of China. Translator John Knoblock called him one of the two or three most important figures in Chinese history. In 213 BC Li advocated burning non-utilitarian texts, a measure that fueled resentment among the educated elite. After Qin Shi Huang's death in 210 BC, Li allied with the eunuch Zhao Gao to install the younger Huhai as emperor. Later accused of treason, he was condemned to death along with his family in 208 BC.

Northern Irish actor. Neeson rose to prominence playing [[Oskar Schindler]] in [[Steven Spielberg]]'s *Schindler's List* (1993), a role that earned him an Academy Award nomination. He has since appeared in films including *Michael Collins* (1996), *Love Actually* (2003) and *Kinsey* (2004), and became an action star with the *Taken* series beginning in 2008. On Broadway he was nominated for Tony Awards for his performances in *Anna Christie* and *The Crucible*. His films have grossed over US$11.7 billion worldwide. He was appointed an Officer of the Order of the British Empire in 2000.

Khitan-led imperial dynasty of China, 916–1125, ruled by the Yelü clan. Founded after the collapse of the [[Tang dynasty]] by Abaoji, the Liao at its greatest extent ruled [[Manchuria]], the Mongolian Plateau, the northern Korean Peninsula, southern Siberia and the northern tip of the North China Plain, including the Sixteen Prefectures around present-day [[Beijing]]. In 1004 the Liao launched an expedition against the Northern Song. After heavy fighting, the Chanyuan Treaty obliged the Song to recognize the Liao as peers and began about 120 years of peace. The Jurchen-led [[Jin dynasty (1115–1234)|Jin dynasty]] destroyed the Liao in 1125. Remaining loyalists under Yelü Dashi founded the Western Liao, which ruled parts of [[Central Asia]] for almost a century before the [[Mongol Empire]] conquered it. Liao cultural achievements are considerable, but the extent of their influence on later developments, such as music and theater, remains debated.

American pianist, singer and actor. Born in [[Wisconsin]] to Italian and Polish parents, he had a four-decade career in concerts, recordings and television. He was the highest-paid entertainer in the world from the 1950s to the 1970s, with concert residencies in Las Vegas. Critics were divided on his flashy showmanship. In 1959 he won a libel suit against the *Daily Mirror* over an article implying he was homosexual, which was then criminalized. He continued to deny it. In 1982 his former lover and chauffeur, Scott Thorson, sued him for palimony. He died of AIDS-related cytomegalovirus pneumonia.

Major [[Conservatism|conservative]] party in Japan, formed in 1955 from a merger of the Liberal Party and the Japan Democratic Party. The party has governed almost continuously since then, apart from 1993–94 and 2009–12. It is often described as a big tent party whose factions range from moderate conservatism to far-right positions. Its platform has supported increased defense spending, close ties with the United States and revising Article 9 of the Constitution. In 2026 it won 316 seats in the House of Representatives, the most in Japanese electoral history.

Country on the West African coast, officially the Republic of Liberia. It is bordered by [[Sierra Leone]], [[Guinea]], [[Ivory Coast]] and the [[Atlantic Ocean]]; its capital and largest city is [[Monrovia]]. Covering 111,369 square kilometers, it has a population of around 5.5 million. Liberia began in the early 19th century as a project of the American Colonization Society, which resettled Black Americans from the [[United States]] in Africa. Its settlers, the Americo-Liberians, declared independence on July 26, 1847, and the U.S. recognized it only in 1862. Liberia was the first African republic to gain independence and is Africa's oldest continuously independent country. It was spared the [[Scramble for Africa]] and was a founding member of the [[United Nations]]. A 1980 coup ended Americo-Liberian rule, and two civil wars from 1989 to 2003 caused about 250,000 deaths. Mining is a major economic driver.

Political philosophy holding liberty and personal sovereignty as its primary values. Most libertarians accept the non-aggression principle, under which individuals may live as they choose as long as they do not initiate force or fraud against others. Libertarians generally oppose state power, warfare, militarism and nationalism, though they differ on the scope of that opposition. Scholars often distinguish left-libertarians, who support an egalitarian redistribution of natural resources, from right-libertarians. The term originated in France, where the libertarian communist Joseph Déjacque used it in an 1857 letter to [[Pierre-Joseph Proudhon]]. Murray Rothbard and Robert Nozick popularized it in the United States, where it became associated with the right. Nozick's *Anarchy, State, and Utopia* (1974) proposed a minimal state in response to [[John Rawls]].

Romantic painting by [[Eugène Delacroix]], commemorating the July Revolution of 1830 that toppled King Charles X. The allegorical figure of Liberty, bare-breasted and wearing a Phrygian cap, leads a mixed group of fighters over a barricade of corpses, holding the tricolor in one hand and a musket with a bayonet in the other. The fighters come from several social classes, from a top-hatted bourgeois to a boy with pistols. Delacroix painted it in autumn 1830, and it was first shown at the Paris Salon of 1831. The French government bought it for 3,000 francs, but it was removed from the Luxembourg Palace because of its political message. It is now in the [[Louvre]]. The painting is sometimes wrongly thought to depict the French Revolution of 1789.

Great library of ancient [[Alexandria]], Egypt, part of the Mouseion, a research institution dedicated to the Muses. The idea may have been proposed to [[Ptolemy I Soter]], but the library was probably built under his son, Ptolemy II Philadelphus, who acquired papyrus scrolls aggressively. Estimates of its holdings range from 40,000 to 700,000 scrolls. Scholars there included [[Eratosthenes]], who calculated the circumference of the earth within a few hundred kilometers, and [[Hero of Alexandria]], who documented the first recorded steam engine. Its influence declined after intellectuals were purged in 145 BC. [[Julius Caesar]] burned part of the collection in 48 BC, but how much was destroyed is unclear. Its end is uncertain, but a Palmyrene invasion between 270 and 275 AD probably destroyed what remained, and the Serapeum annex was demolished in 391 AD.

Research library serving the [[United States Congress]] and the de facto national library of the United States. Founded in 1800 when Congress moved to Washington, it is the oldest federal cultural institution in the country. Its first collection of 740 books, ordered from London, was largely lost in the 1814 burning of Washington during the [[War of 1812]]. [[Thomas Jefferson]] sold his personal library of 6,487 books to restore it, but a fire in 1851 destroyed two-thirds of those books. In 1870 the library gained the right to receive two copies of every copyrightable work printed in the United States. Its main building was constructed between 1890 and 1897. The Congressional Research Service provides nonpartisan research to Congress. The [[John Adams]] and [[James Madison]] buildings were added later.

Free and open-source office productivity suite developed by The Document Foundation. It was created in 2010 as a fork of OpenOffice.org and covers word processing, spreadsheets, presentations, vector graphics, database management and formula editing. The suite supports the OpenDocument format and is compatible with [[Microsoft Office]] file formats. Its first stable release came in January 2011. It runs on [[Linux]], macOS and Windows, and is the default office suite in many Linux distributions. The Document Foundation estimated about 200 million active users in 2018.

North African country in the [[Maghreb]] region, on the Mediterranean coast. With an area of almost 1.8 million square kilometers, it is the fourth-largest country in Africa. Its capital, Tripoli, lies in the northwest, and the population is about seven million. Phoenician and Greek settlements were followed by Roman rule, and Arab conquest from the 7th century brought Islam. [[Italy]] occupied the country after the Italo-Turkish War of 1911. Libya became an independent kingdom in 1951. A 1969 military coup led by [[Muammar Gaddafi]] overthrew King Idris I, and Gaddafi ruled for 42 years; critics described him as a dictator. He was overthrown and killed in the 2011 civil war, part of the [[Arab Spring]]. Rival governments emerged in 2014, and a 2020 ceasefire has not ended political rivalries that delay elections. Libya has the 10th-largest proven oil reserves in the world.

[[Symbiosis|Symbiotic]] partnership of a [[Fungus|fungus]] with a photosynthetic partner, usually a green [[Algae|alga]] or a [[Cyanobacteria|cyanobacterium]]. The fungus provides structure, protection and access to water and minerals, while the photosynthetic partner produces food for both. Lichens are not plants, and they lack true roots, stems or leaves. They come in crustose, foliose and fruticose growth forms and grow on rock, bark, soil and roofs, from sea level to high alpine elevations. About 20,000 species are known. Lichens are pioneers on freshly exposed rock and help form soil. They are a food source for animals such as [[Reindeer]]. Because they are sensitive to [[Air pollution]], they serve as bioindicators of environmental health.

Method of determining ranges by aiming a [[Laser|laser]] at an object or surface and measuring the time its reflected light takes to return. It can produce high-resolution three-dimensional maps. Lidar is used in [[Surveying]], [[Geology]], [[Archaeology]] and [[Forestry]], in atmospheric research and in autonomous cars. The helicopter Ingenuity used lidar on its flights over [[Mars]]. The first lidar-like system was introduced by the Hughes Aircraft Company in 1961, for satellite tracking, shortly after the invention of the laser.

Local anesthetic of the amino amide type, also known as lignocaine. It works by blocking sodium channels in nerves, so that they cannot conduct signals. It is often mixed with [[Adrenaline|adrenaline]] to prolong its effect and reduce bleeding. As a class Ib [[Arrhythmia|antiarrhythmic]] drug, it is also used to treat ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation. Lidocaine was discovered in 1946, went on sale in 1948 and appears on the World Health Organization's List of Essential Medicines. Injected intravenously, it may cause confusion, low blood pressure and an irregular heart rate.

Assertion believed to be false, made with the intention of deceiving or misleading someone. Unlike metaphor or hyperbole, a lie is explicitly meant to be taken literally. The term carries a negative connotation, and depending on context, lying can bring social, legal or religious sanctions. Perjury, lying under oath, can result in criminal charges. Research suggests that people overestimate the value of nonverbal cues, such as avoiding eye contact, as signs of deception. A black lie is told to harm someone, while a blue lie is told in the name of a group's good. Defamation is a false statement that harms reputation. Philosophers disagree on whether lying is ever justified. [[Immanuel Kant]] held that truthfulness admits no exceptions, while consequentialists allow lies when their benefits outweigh their harms.

Doubly landlocked microstate in the [[Alps]], between [[Switzerland]] and [[Austria]]. Formed in 1719, it became fully independent upon the dissolution of the German Confederation in 1866. It is a monarchy headed by its prince, Hans-Adam II, who has reigned since 1989; a 2003 referendum gave the monarch greater powers, including the power to dismiss the government. Liechtenstein covers just over 160 square kilometers and is Europe's fourth-smallest country. Its capital is [[Vaduz]]. It is a member of the [[United Nations]] and the Council of Europe, but not of the [[European Union]]. It participates in the [[Schengen Area]] and uses the Swiss franc in a customs and monetary union with Switzerland. Its strong financial sector was once associated with a tax haven reputation, which it has worked to shed since a 2008 tax affair.

Statistical measure of the average number of years a person of a given age can expect to live. The most common measure is life expectancy at birth, the mean length of life of a hypothetical cohort exposed to a given year's mortality rates. Early Bronze Age remains indicate a value of 24, and world life expectancy at birth was 73.3 years in 2019. High infant mortality, along with deaths from accidents, epidemics, wars and childbirth, substantially lowers the figure. Because the measure is sensitive to infant deaths, a low value does not mean that few people reach old age. It differs from [[Longevity|longevity]], the long lifespan of some individuals. The French woman [[Jeanne Calment]] is verified to have lived 122 years and 164 days.

Sentence of imprisonment for the rest of a convicted person's natural life, with or without the possibility of parole. Such sentences are generally reserved for serious, usually violent crimes. Common law [[Murder|murder]] carries a mandatory life sentence in several countries, including some U.S. states. In [[Sweden]] a life sentence may be commuted to a fixed term after a successful application. [[Portugal]] was the first country to abolish life imprisonment, in 1884. In [[Tasmania]], Martin Bryant received 35 life sentences plus 1,035 years without parole for the 1996 [[Port Arthur massacre]].

Scientific investigation of whether life has existed on [[Mars]]. No conclusive evidence of past or present life has been found. Mars may have had liquid water and habitable conditions in the ancient Noachian period, but habitable conditions do not prove life. Rovers including [[Curiosity (rover)|Curiosity]] have searched for water, organic compounds and biosignatures. In 2018 [[NASA]] detected seasonal variation in [[Methane|methane]] levels, which could come from microorganisms or geological processes. In September 2025 NASA reported a possible biosignature in a rock called Cheyava Falls, though abiotic explanations remain possible. Any life would most likely be preserved underground, away from surface radiation and toxic perchlorates.

Force perpendicular to the direction of flow of a surrounding fluid. A fluid flowing around an object exerts a force on it; lift is the component perpendicular to the oncoming flow, while [[Drag (physics)|drag]] is the component parallel to it. Lift conventionally acts upward to counter gravity, but it can act in any direction perpendicular to the flow. In air it is called aerodynamic force, and in water, hydrodynamic force. Lift is commonly associated with [[Wing|wings]] of [[Fixed-wing aircraft|fixed-wing aircraft]], but it is also generated by propellers, helicopter rotors, [[Sail|sails]] and wind turbines. Simplified explanations based on [[Bernoulli's principle]] are incomplete, and some contain incorrect elements. [[Buoyancy]], by contrast, does not require movement.

Professional [[Association football|association football]] league in [[Mexico]], the highest level of the Mexican league system. Its 18 clubs play two tournaments each season, the Apertura from July to December and the Clausura from January to May. Champions are decided in a knockout phase called the Liguilla. Promotion and relegation have been suspended since 2020. Known as Liga MX since 2012, the league was previously the Primera División Profesional de México. América has won the most titles, sixteen, and 24 clubs have been champions. In 2014–15 the league averaged 25,557 spectators, the largest average attendance of any football league in the Americas, according to CONCACAF.
